Dev Haunt situates the portfolio inside a haunted house — a moonlit exterior establishes the scene, warm light spills from windows, and the content unfolds as a playful supernatural story rather than a conventional professional document. The tone is fun and imaginative, making it one of the most character-rich themes in the Spooky & Magical category.

## Theme Overview

Dev Haunt constructs an atmospheric haunted-house scene as the backdrop for the portfolio — a detailed moonlit exterior with architectural silhouette detail, glowing windows that suggest habitation and warmth, and an overall environment that feels like the set of a beloved Halloween story. The supernatural storytelling is playful rather than frightening, and the portfolio content is woven into the narrative so that visiting feels like exploring the house rather than reading a resume. The combination of illustrated atmosphere and readable content gives the theme remarkable personality.

## Design Highlights

- Moonlit haunted-house exterior scene establishing an immersive atmospheric backdrop
- Warm glowing window light that creates visual depth and a sense of welcoming habitation
- Playful supernatural storytelling tone threaded through content presentation and copy
- Illustrated or stylized architectural silhouette details that make the scene feel realized
- Narrative-driven layout that treats the portfolio as a story to be explored rather than a document to be read

## Who This Theme Suits

Dev Haunt is ideal for developers who want a portfolio with strong personality and a sense of humor — those who enjoy Halloween, horror aesthetics, or whimsical storytelling, and who want visitors to leave their site having had a genuinely enjoyable experience. It works well for frontend developers, game developers, creative coders, and anyone building in public who wants their personal brand to be warm and memorable.

<Tip>The haunted-house narrative works best when your portfolio copy leans into it a little — describing yourself as the "resident developer" or referring to projects as "things currently haunting this house" can extend the metaphor in a way that feels coherent and fun rather than forced.</Tip>
